security_audit.summary: Most detections are documentation syntax, secure examples, or reference URLs and are false positives. Confirmed risks include remote installers, Docker socket exposure, unsafe permissions, token exposure, mutable images, and ineffective CI gates.

remediation.issue: Remote scripts are piped directly into a shell.
remediation.suggestion: Download a versioned release, verify its checksum or signature, inspect it, and execute the verified local file.

remediation.issue: Examples expose the host Docker socket and weaken its permissions.
remediation.suggestion: Use isolated rootless runners without host socket mounts. Never make the Docker socket world-writable or run scanners as root.

remediation.issue: Mutable actions and container tags receive repository privileges.
remediation.suggestion: Pin actions to commit hashes and images to digests. Limit token permissions for every job and third-party action.

remediation.issue: CI behavior does not consistently enforce declared severity thresholds.
remediation.suggestion: Remove blanket success overrides and fail explicitly when parsed results meet the configured critical or high threshold.

content.value_statement: Security flaws and exposed secrets can cross language boundaries and reach production. This skill guides Horusec scans, result triage, and CI integration.
actual_capabilities: Guides Horusec scans across more than 18 supported programming and configuration languages.
Explains text, JSON, and SonarQube-compatible output formats.
Provides GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, and Jenkins integration examples.
Covers git history secret detection, credential rotation, and remediation tracking.
Shows ignore rules, custom rule paths, severity thresholds, and timeout settings.
Includes reusable CI pipeline and security rule templates.
limitations: Horusec, Docker, Git, or equivalent local dependencies must already be available.
Scanner quality depends on upstream tools, rules, language support, and repository context.
Findings require human validation because static analysis can miss issues or report false positives.
Bundled installation and Docker examples require security hardening before production use.

use_cases.title: Review code before commit
use_cases.description: Run a local Horusec scan, prioritize severe findings, and confirm fixes before code review.

use_cases.title: Add security gates to CI
use_cases.description: Configure structured scan output, artifact retention, and enforceable severity thresholds for pull requests.

use_cases.title: Investigate exposed secrets
use_cases.description: Scan repository history, identify affected credentials, plan rotation, and document remediation decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a repository scan
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this repository for Horusec. Identify prerequisites, request approval before execution, then summarize findings by severity and file.

prompt_templates.title: Triage an existing report
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Horusec report. Group findings by severity, identify likely false positives, and propose verified remediation priorities.

prompt_templates.title: Design a CI security gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Horusec CI plan for this repository. Pin dependencies, protect reports, and enforce critical and high severity thresholds.

prompt_templates.title: Tune a monorepo security program
prompt_templates.prompt: Design Horusec coverage for this monorepo. Define project scopes, custom rules, exclusions, timeout controls, ownership, and measurable remediation gates.

output_examples.input: Scan this Python service and prioritize the results.
output: Critical: one exposed credential requires immediate rotation and history cleanup.
High: two injection paths require parameterized database queries.
Next step: remediate confirmed findings, document accepted risks, and rescan.

output_examples.input: Plan Horusec integration for pull requests.
output: Run scans on pull requests with pinned dependencies and minimal permissions.
Store restricted reports for thirty days and redact sensitive snippets.
Block merges on confirmed critical or high findings after validated parsing.

output_examples.input: Reduce false positives without hiding risk.
output: Validate each candidate against source context and exploitability.
Record accepted hashes with owner, rationale, review date, and expiration.
Reassess exclusions after rule updates or major application changes.

best_practices: Pin actions, scanner versions, and container images to immutable revisions.
Run scanners in isolated environments with minimal filesystem, network, and token permissions.
Protect reports as sensitive artifacts and verify every suppression through documented review.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe downloaded scripts directly into a shell.
Do not expose a world-writable Docker socket or run scanners as root.
Do not suppress scanner failures without a reliable parsed severity gate.

faq.question: Which languages does this skill cover?
faq.answer: The guide lists more than 18 languages, including Python, Java, JavaScript, Go, Terraform, Kubernetes, and Shell.

faq.question: Does Horusec require Docker?
faq.answer: Docker is the primary workflow, but Horusec can run locally when all required analyzer dependencies are installed.

faq.question: Can it detect secrets in git history?
faq.answer: Yes. The guide covers history analysis, credential rotation, repository cleanup, and incident documentation.

faq.question: Can scans block a CI build?
faq.answer: Yes. Configure explicit result parsing and tested severity thresholds instead of relying on suppressed command exit codes.

faq.question: How should false positives be handled?
faq.answer: Validate source context, document the acceptance reason, assign an owner, and review ignored findings regularly.

faq.question: Are scan reports sensitive?
faq.answer: Yes. Reports may contain source snippets, paths, and exposed secrets, so restrict access and retention.
